text: In Redux, a ________ is a function that takes the current state and an action and returns the new state.

Creating a new object instead of changing the old one is called an ________ update.
Passing props down through many layers, which a shared store avoids, is called prop ________.
Redux Toolkit uses the ________ library so reducers can be written as if they changed state in place.
A function that reads or derives a value from the store is called a ________.

What is application state, and where should it live?
key_facts: ["state is data that can change and affects what the UI shows", "keep state as close as possible to the components that use it", "move it up or into a shared store only when several distant components need it"]

text: How does Redux manage state?
key_facts: ["all the state lives in one store", "components dispatch actions that describe what happened", "pure reducers compute the new state, and components subscribe to the parts they need"]

text: Why is immutability important in state management?
key_facts: ["change detection can compare references instead of deep values", "old states stay unchanged, which allows undo and time-travel debugging", "changing state in place can stop the UI from updating"]

text: How would you handle data fetched from a server in a front-end app?
key_facts: ["treat it as server state, separate from UI state", "use a library such as TanStack Query or SWR for caching, loading and error states, and refetching", "invalidate or refetch after changes so the UI stays in sync with the server"]

text: When would you choose Redux, Context or local state?
key_facts: ["local state for data used by one component or a small subtree", "Context for values that change rarely but many components read, such as the theme or the user", "a store such as Redux for large shared state that changes often and needs clear update rules and dev tools"]

text: Loading images only when they are about to scroll into view is called ________ loading.

Google's built-in tool that scores page performance is ________.
The Core Web Vital that measures layout jumps is Cumulative Layout ________.
The Core Web Vital that measures when the main content appears is Largest Contentful ________.
Splitting a bundle so code loads only when it is needed is called code ________.
Removing unused exports from a bundle is called tree ________.

________ is a compression format that usually makes text files smaller than gzip.

Why does web performance matter?
key_facts: ["slow pages make users leave before the page loads", "speed affects search ranking through the Core Web Vitals", "faster pages use less data and battery on phones"]

text: What are the Core Web Vitals, and what does each measure?
key_facts: ["Largest Contentful Paint measures how fast the main content appears", "Interaction to Next Paint measures how quickly the page responds to input", "Cumulative Layout Shift measures how much the layout jumps while loading"]

text: How would you make images load faster?
key_facts: ["compress them and use modern formats such as WebP or AVIF", "serve the right size with srcset and sizes", "lazy-load images below the fold and serve them through a CDN"]

text: How would you reduce the JavaScript cost of a large single-page app?
key_facts: ["measure the bundle with a bundle analyzer to find large dependencies", "split code by route and load features only when needed", "remove unused code and libraries, and defer scripts that are not needed at first"]

text: How would you find and fix a slow page load?
key_facts: ["measure with Lighthouse or WebPageTest and read the request waterfall", "find the biggest costs: slow server response, render-blocking files, large images or scripts", "fix the largest first, for example with caching, compression, a CDN or smaller bundles, then measure again"]
